content.comment_body: I'm new to this forum and have searched here and online but couldn't find a solution to my issue. I have several [article_no] modules and a serial cable, running [product_name] version [version_no]. When I try to connect to the module, I get a message saying "unable to connect to IP address COM1," which seems to be a common error, yet there's no clear fix available. I've tried on two different computers—one with Windows 10 64-bit and another with Windows 7 32-bit—and the result is always the same. The serial port is definitely COM1; there are no other options. From what I understand, you don't need to configure the module to start communication; it should begin once the physical connection via the COM port is established. Is that correct? I'm trying to determine if the problem is related to the connection, the module, or the computer itself. Could it be that the computer isn't allowing [product_name] to access COM1, regardless of whether the module is connected? Or does this message mean that no module is responding to a request sent through the COM port? Any advice or suggestions would be appreciated.

Are you sure your message is about connecting to an IP address? That typically refers to an Ethernet connection. First, make sure to select the [product_name] cable option, then choose the correct COM port for your cable. You can identify the correct COM port using your PC's hardware manager, especially if you're using a USB cable. Regards, [user_name]

This error occurs when trying to reach a [product_name] device via the "[product_name] Cable" option and the selected interface—in this case, COM1—but the device can't be accessed (see attachment). I use a PC with Windows 7, [product_name] V[version_no], and an original serial cable from [company_name]. My PC doesn't have a native serial COM port, so I use a USB-to-RS232 converter with an FTDI chipset. When I plug the converter into a USB port, the PC creates a virtual COM port. Using this virtual COM port, I can successfully connect to my [article_no] module without issues.

Hello, It looks like the converter might be the source of the problem. Try these steps: + Open your system's control panel and go to Device Manager, then expand the COM & LPT section. + Connect your converter to the PC and observe which entry is added. + The correct COM port for your converter will be listed there. After that, start [product_name], try to connect, select the USB cable option, and choose the correct COM port as identified above. Hope this helps.

From my experience, [user_name] is correct. The FTDI chip in a converter often causes issues because Windows updates the driver to the official one, and if you use a USB-to-RS232 converter with a non-original or counterfeit FTDI chip, the updated driver blocks these fake chips. You can search online, such as on Google, for solutions to roll back the driver for non-original FTDI chips. [url] Alternatively, you may want to buy a genuine USB/RS232 converter to avoid these problems.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are experiencing ongoing difficulty connecting their PC to [product_name] modules via serial (COM) connection, using [product_name] software and specific hardware versions. Common errors, such as failure to connect to COM1, persist across multiple computers and operating systems, causing confusion and frustration. Discussion focuses on USB-to-RS232 converter reliability, especially issues with counterfeit FTDI chipsets and driver compatibility updates that prevent successful connections. Users seek clarification on diagnosing whether problems are due to the computer, cable, or module.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect reliable, simple communication between their PC and [product_name] modules through a COM port or a USB-to-RS232 converter, without needing complex troubleshooting. They also desire clear diagnostic information or troubleshooting steps when connection problems occur.
